model: Orbital Economy v7.7.19 Nominal Anchor candidate r1
note: Task 045: one new key parameter and one updated key parameter. Merge parameters into accepted annotations on promotion; other entries remain unchanged.

Labor Demand Wage Elasticity.role: KEY PARAMETER: labor-demand wage elasticity ε=1.5; nominal anchor controlling long-run wage-level drift and the A → B population shift.
Labor Demand Wage Elasticity.effect: Only when Labor Market Enabled = 1, each regional Total Labor Requirement = its former food-wrapped formula × (regional Wage / Initial Wage)^(-1.5). Cheaper labor creates more jobs per unit of output, raises employment and the wage bill and feeds back through labor tightness; with the labor market disabled the original formula applies exactly.
Labor Demand Wage Elasticity.evidence: docs/research/NOMINAL_ANCHOR_2026-10-23_RU.md: alternative ε=0.5/1/1.5/2 versus wage norms and hybrid over 80 years; docs/tasks/045-nominal-anchor/V7_7_19_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC.md §§1–5; owner decision 2026-10-23 chooses ε=1.5.

Target Labor Tightness.role: KEY PARAMETER: target ratio of smoothed labor demand to labor force; value remains 0.95.
Target Labor Tightness.effect: Controls the target ratio of smoothed labor demand to labor force, 0.95. Above/below the target wages rise/fall; from v7.7.19 the changed wage also increases/decreases labor demand through Labor Demand Wage Elasticity, feeding back into employment and labor tightness, so tightness converges through labor demand as well as the wage. Value remains 0.95.
Target Labor Tightness.evidence: docs/research/SENSITIVITY_2026-10-10_RU.md: Target Labor Tightness grows from moderate short-horizon sensitivity to a strong long-horizon wage driver; owner decision 2026-10-11 keeps 0.95 unchanged and marks it as a key parameter. See also docs/research/NOMINAL_ANCHOR_2026-10-23_RU.md and docs/tasks/045-nominal-anchor/V7_7_19_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC.md §5 (wage → labor demand negative feedback, owner decision 2026-10-23).
